HOW WE WORK

Less uncertainty.
More clarity.

A review should help you make better decisions, not frighten you into buying services you do not need.

Start with evidence

A newsletter platform, an old supplier incident or a missing public detail does not prove your practice is vulnerable. We distinguish what has been observed, what has been checked and what remains unknown.

A useful finding contains

  • The affected account or process.
  • Evidence and date of the observation.
  • Scope and limitations of the check.
  • A practical action and a named owner.

Keep control of access

The initial conversation does not need client records or passwords. Any later review requires a written scope and agreement on the minimum access necessary.

Boundaries that matter

  • No unsolicited intrusion or credential testing.
  • No sharing client notes for a sales assessment.
  • No testing of supplier systems without their authorisation.
  • No guarantee of compliance, certification or complete security.

Work with the tools you already have

Check authentication, permissions, integrations and recovery before considering migration. A move to a different email or booking provider should solve a demonstrated problem and account for cost, functionality, consent and data handling.

Existing IT providers remain important partners. The review should clarify who owns each action rather than duplicate their work.

About Cyber Defender

Cyber Defender is developing a focused service for independent therapy practices. We do not claim a long trading history, accreditations, an established insurance partnership or a delivery team that has not been confirmed. Service availability and the people responsible for delivery will be confirmed before accepting engagements.
